answers.stem_only: Put a CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket (origin access control) and load the images through the distribution, so edge locations cache the rarely changing images close to users in Asia and Europe.

Use a CloudFront origin group with the us-east-1 bucket as primary and the replicated us-west-2 bucket as secondary, failing over on 5xx status codes; read-only GET/HEAD traffic suits origin failover and needs no custom code.
One CloudFront distribution with two origins: the S3 bucket for the default cache behavior (cached) and the ALB for a /api/* cache behavior with caching disabled (CachingDisabled policy).
CloudFront signed cookies set after sign-in with an expiration: they cover many files (all HLS segments) without changing the requested URLs, unlike signed URLs.

Narrow the cache key with a cache policy that includes only the lang query string (no cookies, no headers), and turn on Origin Shield in the Region closest to the origin to collapse requests from many edge locations and cut origin load.

AWS Global Accelerator with an endpoint group per Region holding the ALB: two static anycast IPs for the partner allow lists, and health-check-based failover that does not depend on DNS caching; CloudFront origin failover does not apply to POST.
A CloudFront Functions function on the viewer request event: lightweight header-based URL rewrite on every request, cheapest option at high volume; Lambda@Edge is more expensive and not needed.

Cache busting: put a version or content hash in the JS/CSS file names on each deployment with long TTLs, and give index.html a short TTL so it points to the new names; no invalidations needed and browser/proxy copies are bypassed.
Use CloudFront VPC origins: move to an internal ALB in private subnets and add it as a VPC origin, so the ALB is no longer internet-facing and only CloudFront can reach it.

Put a CloudFront distribution in front of the bucket and use its domain in the download links: edge caching serves the millions of repeat downloads, S3-to-CloudFront transfer is free and CloudFront data transfer out costs less than S3 direct.

Lambda@Edge on the viewer request event, because the check must run on every request (including cache hits) and must call DynamoDB over the network, which CloudFront Functions cannot do; origin request would run only on cache misses.

AWS Global Accelerator in front of the two NLBs (endpoint group per Region): supports UDP, gives two static anycast IPs for allow lists, and carries traffic over the AWS backbone from the nearest edge.
Large, weekly changing HTTPS downloads are cacheable content: a CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs caches the patch files at edge locations near players for the lowest latency.
Add an HTTPS listener to the ALB with an ACM certificate for origin.example.com requested in the ALB's Region (eu-central-1), and set the CloudFront origin protocol policy to HTTPS only.
A Minimum TTL above 0 overrides the origin's Cache-Control no-cache/no-store/private; set the cache policy's Minimum TTL to 0 (or use CachingDisabled) for /api/* so the origin headers decide.

Restrict the ALB security group to the AWS-managed CloudFront origin-facing prefix list, and have CloudFront add a secret custom origin header that an ALB listener rule requires (other requests get a fixed 403), so only this distribution's requests pass.

Add a us-west-2 endpoint group with the standby NLB to the same listener and set its traffic dial to 0% (us-east-1 at 100%): normal traffic goes only to us-east-1, and failover to a group with healthy weighted endpoints ignores the traffic dial.

Origin access control on the S3 origin (supports PUT/DELETE dynamic requests, unlike the legacy OAI), allow the PUT method in the cache behavior, and a bucket policy granting the CloudFront service principal for this distribution s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject; keep Block Public Access on.
Origin access control on the S3 origin plus a bucket policy that allows only the CloudFront service principal with the distribution ARN as source; no signed URLs, since every visitor may download.
CloudFront requires its viewer certificate in ACM in us-east-1 (N. Virginia); the ALB requires its certificate in its own Region, ap-southeast-2.
Set the us-east-1 endpoint group traffic dial to 0% so new connections go to us-west-2, let existing connections drain, patch, then set the dial back to 100%.
Keep OAC, add a trusted key group to the cache behavior, and have the application issue a short-lived CloudFront signed URL for each file after it confirms the payment.
